critique: The render has a plausible warm magical-particle look on black, with a dense glowing core and fine spark scatter. Motion between t1 and t4 does show active upward dispersion. However, it reads as a small upward fountain/crown rather than a coherent magic disc: the particle mass is vertically V-shaped, lacks a broad circular/elliptical disc silhouette, and occupies too little of the frame. The time-driven color sweep also makes the entire effect abruptly change from pale yellow at t1 to saturated orange at t4 instead of maintaining a stable luminous disc palette.

suggestions.why: Removing the strong upward gravity will stop the crown/fountain trajectory and preserve a flatter disc-like particle field.
A substantially wider directional spread will distribute particles radially into a disc/halo silhouette rather than a narrow upward fan.
Larger particles will give the magic disc a more visible, substantial luminous body at the current small on-screen scale.
Use a stable warm gold/orange birth color instead of globally sweeping every particle from yellow to orange across the sampled frames.
